output_json.patch_notes:
1) agent/core/src/main/java/org/jolokia/util/IoUtil.java: added a CALLBACK_PATTERN regex, public isValidCallback()/validateCallback() helpers, and a validateCallback() call at the top of streamResponseAndClose() (shared streaming sink used by both AgentServlet and JolokiaHttpHandler).
2) agent/core/src/main/java/org/jolokia/http/AgentServlet.java: sendResponse() now calls IoUtil.validateCallback(callback) immediately after extracting the 'callback' request parameter, before it's used to pick the content type or build the JSONP body in sendStreamingResponse()/sendAllJSON() — this single call covers both response variants.
3) agent/jvm/src/main/java/org/jolokia/jvmagent/handler/JolokiaHttpHandler.java: sendResponse() (the dispatcher used by both sendStreamingResponse() and sendAllJSON()) now validates the 'callback' parameter from the ParsedUri before dispatching, closing the same class of bug in the JVM agent.
4) Added regression tests: IoUtilTest (valid/invalid callback name checks + streamResponseAndClose rejecting a malicious callback), AgentServletTest (doGet with a malicious callback now throws IllegalArgumentException instead of reflecting it), JolokiaHttpHandlerTest (doHandle with a percent-encoded malicious callback throws IllegalArgumentException). Existing tests using legitimate callback names ('myCallback', 'data') are unaffected since they match the new identifier pattern.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change: callback names that aren't valid (optionally dotted) JavaScript identifiers (e.g. containing spaces, quotes, angle brackets, parens) are now rejected with IllegalArgumentException instead of being reflected into the response — this is only reachable by malformed/malicious input, not legitimate JSONP usage, and is handled via the same generic error paths (uncaught RuntimeException surfaced by the servlet container / HttpServer) already used for other invalid-input cases in these classes (e.g. unsupported HTTP method). No change to behavior for well-formed callback names. Note: in this sandboxed build environment, all JolokiaHttpHandlerTest cases (including ones unrelated to this change, e.g. testCallbackGet, invalidMethod) fail with a pre-existing NullPointerException from `com.sun.net.httpserver.Headers.set(name, null)` under this JDK's stricter header validation — verified this occurs identically on the unpatched baseline (via git stash), so it's an unrelated environment/JDK issue, not a regression from this patch. The equivalent core-module tests (IoUtilTest, AgentServletTest) pass cleanly and exercise the same shared validation logic used by JolokiaHttpHandler.
output_json.summary: Fixed reflected XSS (CWE-079) in Jolokia's JSONP callback handling. The 'callback' request parameter was reflected verbatim, unescaped, into the response body (wrapped as `callback(...)`) with a text/javascript content type, across both the servlet (AgentServlet) and JVM-agent (JolokiaHttpHandler) code paths, for both the streaming (IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose) and non-streaming (sendAllJSON) response variants. An attacker-controlled callback name such as `"></script><script>alert(1)</script>` would be echoed directly into the response, enabling script injection. Root-caused the fix by adding a shared validator (IoUtil.isValidCallback/validateCallback) that restricts callback names to valid, optionally-dotted JavaScript identifiers ([a-zA-Z0-9_$]+(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_$]+)*), and invoking it at the single choke point in each response path: AgentServlet#sendResponse (covers both its streaming and non-streaming branches) and JolokiaHttpHandler#sendResponse (covers its streaming and non-streaming branches too), plus defense-in-depth inside IoUtil#streamResponseAndClose itself since it's shared by both agents. Invalid callback names now cause an IllegalArgumentException instead of being reflected, which is handled the same way other malformed-request errors already are in these classes (safe error response, no attacker content reflected).
